description: Telecommunications, software-as-a-service (SaaS), recurring subscriptions, monthly recurring revenue, customer churn, and subscriber lifetime value.

kpi_templates.name: Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR)
kpi_templates.description: Normalized monthly recurring subscription revenue across active subscribers.
kpi_templates.sql_template: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM({monetary_recurring}) AS DOUBLE), 2) AS metric_value FROM df

kpi_templates.name: Average Revenue Per User (ARPU)
kpi_templates.description: Average monthly recurring revenue generated per subscriber.
kpi_templates.sql_template: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG({monetary_recurring}) AS DOUBLE), 2) AS metric_value FROM df

kpi_templates.name: Customer Churn Rate
kpi_templates.description: Percentage of subscribers that have cancelled or churned.
kpi_templates.sql_template: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(CAST({churn_flag} AS VARCHAR)) IN ('1', 'yes', 'true') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DOUBLE), 2) AS metric_value FROM df

kpi_templates.name: Active Subscribers
kpi_templates.description: Total count of active, non-churned subscriber accounts.
kpi_templates.sql_template: SELECT CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT {subscriber_id}) AS BIGINT) AS metric_value FROM df

kpi_templates.name: Average Tenure
kpi_templates.description: Average customer relationship duration in months.
kpi_templates.sql_template: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG({tenure}) AS DOUBLE), 1) AS metric_value FROM df

dimensional_templates.description: Subscriber count and recurring revenue distribution by contract type.
dimensional_templates.sql_template: SELECT CAST({contract_type} AS VARCHAR) AS entity, ROUND(CAST(SUM({monetary_recurring}) AS DOUBLE), 2) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT {subscriber_id}) AS order_count FROM df GROUP BY {contract_type} ORDER BY revenue DESC

dimensional_templates.description: Revenue and subscriber segmentation by service tier.
dimensional_templates.sql_template: SELECT CAST({service_type} AS VARCHAR) AS entity, ROUND(CAST(SUM({monetary_recurring}) AS DOUBLE), 2) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT {subscriber_id}) AS order_count FROM df GROUP BY {service_type} ORDER BY revenue DESC
